label: Enterprise Firewall Core
description: Enterprise Firewall Core (EF-Core) - 2x 1G RJ45 + 1x MGMT RJ45 + 1x Console + 8x 10G RJ45 + 4x 25G SFP28 (25G/10G/1G) + 4x 100G QSFP28 (100G/40G). 171 W max.
notes:
Census read from the vendor's own Port Layout table: https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/ef-core (HTTP 200, 674,322 B, server-rendered, read 2026-11-19) prints six rows - "1 GbE RJ45 = 2 (1G/100M/10M)", "10 GbE RJ45 = 8 (10G/5G/2.5G/1G/100M)", "25G SFP28 = 4 (25G/10G/1G)", "100G QSFP28 = 4 (100G/40G)", "MGMT = 1 (1G/100M/10M)", "Console = 1". Before this correction the row carried only the first two of those and no management or console socket, so a 1U firewall that ships with both had 18 jacks where the unit has 20. The management port is a separate RJ45 on the front panel, not one of the two 1 GbE data ports: the vendor lists it as its own row with its own rate set, and the same table's Management section reads "Ethernet" alongside the 1.3" LCM touchscreen. Both 1 GbE data ports also gain the 10M rung the vendor prints for them. Power, unchanged and confirmed on the same page: "Max. Power Consumption = 171W", "Power Method = Universal AC input, 100-240V AC, 7.5A Max., 50/60 Hz", "Power Supply = (2) Hot-Swappable AC/DC 550W PSU" - no PoE front end, so every copper port here is a plain socket.

Layer 2: Ubiquiti's controller device database classifies this SKU as a switch - https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json (HTTP 200, 832,585 B, read 2026-11-21) lists EF-Core deviceCapabilities GATEWAY, NETWORK_APPLICATION, PROTECT_APPLICATION, SWITCH, CONTROLLER, APPLICATION_MODE, HAS_CLIENTS and draws its panel as `01 03 05 07 09 11 13 __ 15 23 __ 31` / `02 04 06 08 10 12 14 __ 19 27 __ __` - and the vendor tech-spec table publishes the bridge's forwarding database at https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/ef-core (HTTP 200, 674,322 B, read 2026-11-21), which prints "MAC Address Table Size = 130,000" with "LACP Port Aggregation" ticked; no segmentation row appears, so none is claimed. A MAC address table is a bridge FDB; a gateway that only routed would hold neither it nor a LAG. While the row shipped without `l2-forward` its copper sockets were routed interfaces: `switchport access vlan 10` was answered with "cannot switch frames: it has no l2-forward capability", and two hosts on eth2 and eth3 in 192.168.1.0/24 could not resolve each other's ARP ("not addressed to this device"). WAN side unchanged: "Default WAN Ports = (1) 100G QSFP28 / (1) 25G SFP28 / (1) 10 GbE RJ45", "Max. WAN Port Count = 8"; no socket is pinned as WAN.
